accounting.documentRule: Every document listed by each frozen near-deduplicated source manifest is classified exactly once for language and exactly once for primary domain.
accounting.byteRule: Text bytes are exact on-disk UTF-8 byte lengths; no decoding-dependent character count substitutes for bytes.
accounting.percentRule: Percentages are count or byte subtotal divided by the corresponding full-corpus or source total and rounded to six decimal places only for reporting.
accounting.technicalFlagRule: CODE_OR_TECHNICAL_SYNTAX is orthogonal to mutually exclusive language and primary-domain categories and therefore is not included in their reconciliation sums.

languageClassification.classificationType: content-derived; frozen source language labels are reported as lineage priors but do not force a result
languageClassification.tokens: Unicode alphabetic runs of at least two characters

additionalLanguageMarkers.otherScript: Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Han, Hiragana, Katakana, or Hangul alphabetic tokens

languageClassification.score: Marker occurrences are counted. German tokens containing ä, ö, ü or ß add one German evidence point. German tokens ending gesetz, verordnung, ung, keit, heit or schaft add one German evidence point. Non-Latin-script alphabetic tokens count as additional-language evidence.
decisionOrder: MIXED_LANGUAGE when two or more language evidence scores are each at least 3 and the second-highest/highest ratio is at least 0.5
ADDITIONAL_LANGUAGE when additional evidence is at least 3 and either it leads the next score by 2x or non-Latin tokens are at least 20% of alphabetic tokens
ENGLISH when English evidence is at least 3 and leads every other score by at least 2x
GERMAN when German evidence is at least 3 and leads every other score by at least 2x
languageClassification.ambiguityRule: Ties, weak evidence, or insufficient lead remain MIXED or UNKNOWN; source expectations do not break ties.

technicalCodeClassification.sourceRule: All d1-acq001-python-docs-313 documents qualify because the frozen extraction lineage identifies them as software documentation.
technicalCodeClassification.contentRule: Any other document qualifies only if at least two distinct syntax indicators occur: Python prompt >>>, def/class/import/from statements, paired braces/brackets, assignment/operator lines, traceback, or a fenced code block.
technicalCodeClassification.aggregation: One orthogonal flag per document; bytes count the full flagged document.

domainClassification.classificationType: mutually exclusive primary domain; source-derived when lineage is unambiguous, content-derived fallback otherwise
domainClassification.sourceRuleRationale: Python members are software documentation with preserved code examples. Gesetze records contain index titles only; linked legal bodies were not acquired, so classifying them as government prose would overstate their content.
contentFallbackOrder: code/software documentation if technical/code flag is true
science if deterministic science terminology dominates
government/public information if government/legal prose dominates
technical/computing if computing terminology dominates without documentation lineage
structured factual text if record-like fragments dominate
domainClassification.ambiguityRule: Known-source rules take precedence. Unknown-source content ties fail closed rather than being assigned arbitrarily.

plannedComparisons.comparisonBasis: actual byte percentages; MIXED and UNKNOWN are reported separately and are not redistributed into planned buckets
